verdicts.reason: Both scatter the three steps as microscopic, unreadable text (01/02 far left, 03 stranded bottom-right under the CTA) and leave large dead areas. A at least keeps the ULTRA logo as its own mark and the legal under the headline, though the subtitle floats detached at the top. B puts the fine print at the top of the reading order and tacks the logo onto the end of the subtitle as an afterthought, which damages the brand.

A pushes the Shop Ritual Kits button flush against the 'The' of the headline (a near-collision) and puts the steps out of order (02 alone at left, 01 and 03 at right). The step copy is unreadably small in both. B keeps the CTA clear at the right and the steps in sequence, but it still has the detached subtitle, tiny steps and an unbalanced, split layout.

A shows the legal text first at the top and buries the ULTRA logo inline after the subtitle. Its step text is illegible and 03 is isolated, but the CTA sits cleanly on the right. B jams the CTA against the headline and splits the steps out of order (02 left, 01/03 right), with unreadable step copy and the subtitle stranded at the top.

Both butt the CTA against the headline and scramble the step order (02 left, 01/03 right) in unreadable micro-type. A also leads with the fine print at the top and demotes the logo to an inline tag after the subtitle, so nearly every hierarchy rule fails. B at least keeps the subtitle on top, the logo standalone and the legal at the bottom.
